verification.note: Checked at the commit. frontend/src/components/appshell/useMemberTarget.ts:23-26: key is null when target is null or has no kinds, otherwise drive, target id and attempt. Line 27: held is only set at :33 on resolution and is never cleared. Line 41: evaluation = held.evaluation only when held.key === key. Switching A -> default (key null, evaluation null) -> A restores key A-key (attempt is unchanged, since only retry increments it), so evaluation returns the old result with evaluating false and ready true (useVideoApp.ts:104-115 and useReadingApp.ts:121-133 derive evaluating and ready from evaluation === null). The effect at :29-38 then re-runs the evaluation, but the stale result is used in the meantime, so requests carry the old fileIds before this visit's evaluation has succeeded (I8). The docstring at :12-16 says a result that outlives its target is dropped, and the code does not do that. The claim is accurate as stated. The same mechanism also applies to a failed or tooLarge prior result, which would be shown again before re-evaluation.

specification_compliance: I8 is violated in the window after switching a member target back: requests carry members from a previous evaluation before this visit's evaluation succeeds (useMemberTarget.ts:41 with :23-27).
The hook's own docstring (useMemberTarget.ts:12-16) states that a result outliving its target is dropped; the code keeps it.
potential_unspecified_behavior: If the Smart Collection's query was edited between visits while the target id and attempt stayed the same, the stale members could also be shown after the switch back; not checked.
regression_risks: Fixing held-state clearing (for example, keying held by the full key and clearing on key change) must still keep the no-retry-on-same-target behaviour and the retry control's re-evaluation.
test_coverage: Not checked: whether any test in frontend/src/components/__tests__ or videoapp/readingapp test directories covers switching a member target away and back. The read was limited to the source files.
not_verified: No test was run; the claim was verified by reading the code only.
Did not check how useVideoApp / useReadingApp build their listing load keys, so I did not confirm whether a stale fileIds value actually reaches a request or a visible list in the UI.
Did not check whether the page can remount on a target change, which would reset held state (I read the hook as persisting across target changes).
Did not check whether the window of stale results can be observed in practice, or how long a re-evaluation normally takes.
